examples.ko: 어릴 때 텔레비전에서 단막극을 자주 봤어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I often watched one-act dramas on TV.

examples.ko: 이 단막극은 한 시간 만에 끝나서 보기 편해요.
examples.en: This one-act drama ends in an hour, so it's easy to watch.

examples.ko: 단막극 한 편으로 신인 배우가 유명해졌어요.
examples.en: The newcomer actor became famous through a single one-act drama.

examples.ko: 학교 축제에서 우리 반이 단막극을 올렸어요.
examples.en: At the school festival, our class staged a one-act play.
One-act dramas have become rare these days, which is a pity.

examples.ko: 그 단막극에서 아버지 역을 맡은 배우가 최고였어요.
examples.en: The actor who played the father in that one-act drama was the best.

explain: 한 편으로 끝나는 짧은 극이라서, 여러 회로 이어지는 '연속극'과 자주 비교돼요. 연극 무대보다는 텔레비전 드라마 이야기에서 더 자주 들려요.
explain_en: Because it finishes in a single episode, it is often contrasted with '연속극' (a serial drama). You hear it more in talk about TV dramas than about stage plays.

examples.ko: 건물 단면도를 보면 층 높이를 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you look at the building's cross-section drawing, you can see the floor heights.
The designer drew a cross-section of the house for me.

examples.ko: 과학 시간에 화산 단면도를 보고 구조를 배웠어요.
examples.en: In science class, we learned the structure by looking at a cross-section of a volcano.

examples.ko: 단면도가 있으니까 안이 어떻게 생겼는지 이해하기 쉬워요.
examples.en: With a cross-section, it's easy to understand what the inside looks like.

examples.ko: 이 책에는 지구의 단면도가 크게 실려 있어요.
examples.en: This book has a large cross-section diagram of the Earth.

examples.ko: 평면도와 단면도를 같이 봐야 정확히 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: You have to look at the floor plan and the cross-section together to understand exactly.

explain: 위에서 내려다본 그림인 '평면도'와 짝으로 자주 나와요. 건축, 과학 교과서, 제품 설명서에서 '지구 단면도', '건물 단면도'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It often appears as a pair with '평면도' (a floor plan seen from above). You see it in architecture, science textbooks and product manuals, as in '지구 단면도' or '건물 단면도'.

examples.ko: 그 내각은 단명해서 반년도 못 갔어요.
examples.en: That cabinet was short-lived and didn't even last half a year.
Trends that are too short-lived are forgotten quickly.
I'm worried this shop will also be short-lived.

examples.ko: 그 브랜드는 단명했지만 팬은 아직도 많아요.
examples.en: That brand was short-lived, but it still has many fans.

examples.ko: 단명했던 그 잡지를 아직 가지고 있어요.
examples.en: I still have that short-lived magazine.

examples.ko: 신문에는 그 회사가 단명할 거라는 기사가 나왔어요.
examples.en: The newspaper ran an article saying the company would be short-lived.

explain: 사람의 수명에도 쓰지만, 정부, 유행, 프로그램처럼 오래 못 가는 것에도 많이 써요. 반대말은 '장수하다'이고, 명사 앞에서는 '단명한'으로 꾸며요.
explain_en: It can describe a person's lifespan, but it is also used a lot for things that don't last, like governments, trends and shows. The opposite is '장수하다', and before a noun you say '단명한'.

en: at once; immediately; on the spot; right away

examples.ko: 그 말을 듣고 단박에 화가 풀렸어요.
examples.en: My anger disappeared the moment I heard those words.
As soon as I saw the problem, I knew the answer right away.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 제 부탁을 단박에 거절했어요.
examples.en: He turned down my request on the spot.

examples.ko: 형은 단박에 일어나서 문을 열어 줬어요.
examples.en: My brother got up at once and opened the door for me.
Even though she said it was expensive, she bought it right away.

examples.ko: 단박에 마음에 드는 집을 찾아서 바로 계약했어요.
examples.en: I found a house I liked right away and signed the contract immediately.

explain: 거의 '단박에' 모양으로 써요. '바로', '당장'과 비슷하지만 망설임 없이 한 번에 해 버리는 느낌이 있어서, 결정하거나 이해하거나 거절할 때 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It almost always appears as '단박에'. It is close to '바로' or '당장', but it carries a feel of doing something in one go without hesitation, so it suits deciding, understanding or refusing.

examples.ko: 이번 행사는 단발성이라 다음 계획은 없어요.
examples.en: This event is a one-off, so there are no plans for the next one.
We need steady support rather than one-time events.
That accident was not a one-time problem.
I'm looking for a one-off part-time job.

examples.ko: 정책이 단발성에 그치면 효과가 오래가지 않아요.
examples.en: If a policy ends up being a one-time thing, its effect doesn't last long.

examples.ko: 이 기사는 단발성으로 끝나지 않고 연재될 거예요.
examples.en: This article won't end as a one-off but will run as a series.

explain: 반대말은 '지속적', '연속적'이에요. 행사, 이벤트, 정책, 뉴스에서 자주 쓰고, '단발성 행사'처럼 명사 앞에 붙여서도 말해요.
explain_en: Its opposites are '지속적' and '연속적'. It is common with events, policies and news, and you can attach it before a noun, as in '단발성 행사'.

examples.en: It's hard to improve your skills in a short time.

examples.ko: 단시일 내에 일을 끝내야 해서 바빠요.
examples.en: I have to finish the work in a short time, so I'm busy.

examples.ko: 살은 단시일에 빼면 다시 찌기 쉬워요.
examples.en: If you lose weight in a short time, it's easy to gain it back.

examples.ko: 이 프로젝트는 단시일에 끝낼 수 없어요.
examples.en: This project can't be finished in a short time.
Many people applied within a short period.
There's no way to learn Korean in a short time.

explain: '단시일에', '단시일 내에'처럼 거의 정해진 모양으로 써요. 반대는 '장기간'이고, 말할 때는 '짧은 시간에', '금방'이라고 더 자주 해요.
explain_en: It nearly always appears in set forms like '단시일에' or '단시일 내에'. The opposite is '장기간', and in casual speech people more often say '짧은 시간에' or '금방'.

examples.en: At first, that actor only played minor roles.
I appeared briefly in a drama as a bit player.
Even if it's a minor role, I want to act hard.
I heard my friend appeared in a movie in a small part.
Even the bit-part actors gather early at the set.
She started with minor roles and worked up to the lead.

explain: '주연', '조연'과 나란히 나오는 말인데, 단역은 대사가 거의 없거나 잠깐 나오는 역이에요. '단역 배우', '단역을 맡다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It sits alongside '주연' (lead) and '조연' (supporting), but a 단역 is a role with few or no lines or only a brief appearance. You say '단역 배우' or '단역을 맡다'.

examples.ko: 이 단열재는 실내 온도 유지에 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: This insulation material helps keep the room temperature steady.

examples.ko: 겨울에 춥지 않게 벽에 단열재를 넣었어요.
examples.en: We put insulation in the walls so it isn't cold in winter.
If you use good insulation, your heating bill goes down.

examples.ko: 오래된 집은 단열재가 부족해서 외풍이 심해요.
examples.en: Old houses lack insulation, so the drafts are bad.

examples.ko: 어떤 단열재가 가장 좋은지 전문가에게 물어봤어요.
examples.en: I asked an expert which insulation is the best.
The price of insulation went up, so the construction cost increased.

explain: 집을 짓거나 고칠 때 자주 듣는 말이에요. '단열재를 넣다/붙이다'처럼 쓰고, '단열 공사', '단열 창호'처럼 '단열'만 앞에 붙인 말도 많아요.
explain_en: You often hear it when a house is built or renovated. It goes with verbs like '단열재를 넣다/붙이다', and many related terms use just '단열', such as '단열 공사' and '단열 창호'.

examples.ko: 야당 후보 단일화가 오늘 뉴스에 나왔어요.
examples.en: The unification of opposition candidates was in the news today.

examples.ko: 두 회사는 서류 양식의 단일화를 추진하고 있어요.
examples.en: The two companies are pushing to standardize their document formats.

examples.ko: 단일화 협상이 잘 안 풀려서 걱정이에요.
examples.en: I'm worried because the unification talks aren't going well.
Confusion decreased a lot thanks to unifying the rules.
They succeeded in unifying their candidates, and their approval rating rose.

examples.ko: 여러 단체의 단일화는 쉬운 일이 아니에요.
examples.en: Unifying several organizations is not an easy thing.

explain: 선거 뉴스의 '후보 단일화'가 가장 흔해요. 여러 개를 하나로 정리한다는 점에서 '통일'과 비슷하지만, 단일화는 후보, 창구, 양식, 규격처럼 구체적인 것에 많이 써요.
explain_en: The most common use is '후보 단일화' in election news. It is similar to '통일' in turning several things into one, but 단일화 is used more for concrete things such as candidates, contact points, forms and standards.

examples.en: The two parties decided to unify their candidates.
The company unified its inquiry desks into one.
If you standardize the specifications, management is easier.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 연락 방법을 단일화해야 해요.
examples.en: Our team needs to unify how we contact each other.

examples.ko: 서류 양식을 단일화한 뒤로 실수가 줄었어요.
examples.en: Mistakes have decreased since we standardized the document form.
If we don't unify it, confusion will arise.

explain: 'A를 B로 단일화하다'처럼 써요. '통합하다'는 따로 있던 것을 합칠 때 넓게 쓰고, 단일화하다는 후보, 창구, 양식을 하나로 정리할 때 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is used like 'A를 B로 단일화하다'. '통합하다' is broad for merging things that were separate, while 단일화하다 is often used for bringing candidates, contact points or forms down to one.

examples.ko: 그렇게 단정적인 표현을 쓰면 오해할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you use such definitive wording, people may misunderstand.
It's still too early to draw a definitive conclusion.

examples.ko: 그는 단정적인 말투로 자기 생각만 말했어요.
examples.en: He spoke only his own thoughts in a categorical tone.
In the news, you have to be careful with categorical reporting.
He was criticized because of his categorical remarks.
It's hard for me to say it with certainty yet.

explain: 확인하지 않고 딱 잘라 말하는 느낌이라 조금 부정적일 때가 많아요. '단정적인', '단정적으로'처럼 활용하고, 반대 느낌은 '유보적'이에요.
explain_en: It carries a feel of speaking flatly without checking, so it is often a bit negative. It is used as '단정적인' or '단정적으로', and the opposite feel is '유보적' (reserved, non-committal).

examples.en: Please dress neatly in front of adults.
I tied my hair neatly and went to the interview.

examples.ko: 학생들이 교복을 단정히 입고 줄을 섰어요.
examples.en: The students lined up wearing their uniforms neatly.
I tidied up the desk neatly.

examples.ko: 그는 늘 단정히 앉아서 이야기를 들어요.
examples.en: He always sits properly and listens to the story.
Since guests were there, I straightened my appearance neatly.

explain: 옷, 머리, 자세, 정리 상태가 흐트러짐 없이 바를 때 써요. '깔끔하게'와 비슷하지만 단정히는 예의 바르고 반듯한 느낌이 더 강해요. 보통 '입다, 앉다, 하다'와 같이 나와요.
explain_en: Use it when clothes, hair, posture or arrangement are in good order. It is similar to '깔끔하게', but 단정히 has a stronger feel of being proper and well-mannered. It usually goes with verbs like '입다', '앉다' and '하다'.

examples.en: The dancheong of that temple is really colorful.
I took many photos of the dancheong at Gyeongbokgung.

examples.ko: 단청을 새로 해서 건물이 산뜻해 보여요.
examples.en: They repainted the dancheong, so the building looks fresh.

examples.ko: 한국의 전통 건물에는 단청이 칠해져 있어요.
examples.en: Traditional Korean buildings have dancheong painted on them.

examples.ko: 단청 색깔이 바랜 곳은 다시 칠한대요.
examples.en: I hear they will repaint the parts where the dancheong colors have faded.

examples.ko: 외국인 친구에게 단청의 아름다움을 설명해 줬어요.
examples.en: I explained the beauty of dancheong to my foreign friend.

explain: 궁궐이나 절 같은 전통 건물의 처마와 기둥에 그린 색 무늬를 말해요. 여행이나 문화 수업에서 자주 나오고, '단청을 입히다/칠하다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It refers to the colorful patterns painted on the eaves and pillars of traditional buildings such as palaces and temples. It comes up in travel and culture classes, and you say '단청을 입히다/칠하다'.

examples.en: That incident became the starting point of the reform.

examples.ko: 작은 실수가 큰 문제의 단초를 제공했어요.
examples.en: A small mistake provided the seed of a big problem.
The starting point of the research came from an accidental discovery.

examples.ko: 이번 대화가 화해의 단초가 되면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I hope this conversation becomes the start of reconciliation.

examples.ko: 경찰은 사건 해결의 단초를 찾았다고 해요.
examples.en: They say the police found a lead toward solving the case.

examples.ko: 이 메모가 문제를 풀 단초가 될 수 있어요.
examples.en: This memo could be the clue that solves the problem.

explain: '단초가 되다', '단초를 제공하다/찾다'처럼 써요. '실마리'와 비슷하지만 단초는 무언가가 시작되는 계기라는 느낌이 더 강해요. 대화보다는 뉴스나 글에서 더 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It is used as '단초가 되다' or '단초를 제공하다/찾다'. It is close to '실마리' (a clue), but 단초 leans more toward the trigger where something begins. It shows up more in news and writing than in conversation.

examples.en: My family is small because there are few members.
The newlyweds' home had little furniture, so it was simple.
I want to have a small, simple wedding.
My belongings were few, so the move ended quickly.
The table setting is simple, but the taste is really good.
For this trip, I packed my bag light.

explain: 식구, 살림, 짐, 상차림처럼 사람이나 물건의 수가 적고 군더더기가 없을 때 써요. '간단하다'가 복잡하지 않다는 느낌이라면, 단출하다는 가짓수가 적어서 깔끔한 느낌이에요.
explain_en: Use it when the number of people or things is small and there is nothing extra, such as family members, belongings, luggage or a meal. While '간단하다' feels uncomplicated, 단출하다 feels neat because there are few items.

examples.en: My grandmother lives in a one-story house with a yard.
A one-story house has no stairs, so it's comfortable to live in.

examples.ko: 시골에서 작은 단층집을 한 채 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a small one-story house in the countryside.
Most houses in this neighborhood are one-story.
Since it's a one-story house, I don't worry about noise from upstairs.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 살던 단층집이 아직도 생각나요.
examples.en: I still remember the one-story house I lived in as a child.

explain: '이층집'과 대비되는 말이에요. 아파트나 빌라와 달리 한 층으로 된 개인 주택을 떠올리는 말이고, '단층 주택'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It contrasts with '이층집' (a two-story house). It brings to mind a one-floor private home, unlike an apartment or villa, and it can also be called '단층 주택'.

en: be pleased with; welcome (mostly used in the negative)

examples.en: My parents weren't pleased with my decision.

examples.ko: 그는 새로운 일을 달가워하는 눈치가 아니에요.
examples.en: He doesn't seem to welcome the new task.
The kids aren't fond of vegetable side dishes.
It's not news the boss will be happy about.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 제 도움을 달가워했으면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I wish he would welcome my help.

examples.ko: 낯선 음식을 달가워하던 친구도 지금은 잘 먹어요.
examples.en: My friend who didn't like unfamiliar food eats it well now.

explain: 거의 '달가워하지 않다'처럼 부정으로 많이 써요. 누군가의 태도나 반응을 말할 때 쓰기 때문에 주로 '그는, 부모님은' 같은 다른 사람이 주어예요.
explain_en: It is mostly used in the negative, as '달가워하지 않다'. Because it describes someone's attitude or reaction, the subject is usually another person, like '그는' or '부모님은'.

examples.en: That news isn't very welcome to me.
An unwelcome guest suddenly came by.

examples.ko: 달가운 소식이 있으면 바로 알려 주세요.
examples.en: If you have welcome news, please tell me right away.
Even though it was kind, it didn't sound welcome to me.

examples.ko: 솔직히 그 제안이 달갑다고는 말 못 해요.
examples.en: Honestly, I can't say that proposal is welcome.

examples.ko: 달갑지는 않지만 어쩔 수 없이 받아들였어요.
examples.en: I didn't like it, but I had no choice but to accept.

explain: 거의 '달갑지 않다' 모양으로 써요. ㅂ 불규칙이라서 '달가워요, 달가운'으로 바뀌어요. '반갑다'가 기쁜 만남이나 소식에 쓴다면, 달갑다는 마음에 들고 내키는 느낌에 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: It almost always appears as '달갑지 않다'. It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective, so it becomes '달가워요' and '달가운'. While '반갑다' is for happy meetings or news, 달갑다 is about something that feels agreeable and appealing.

examples.en: The dishes clatter against each other when I wash up.

examples.ko: 서랍 안에서 동전이 달그락 소리를 내요.
examples.en: The coins rattle inside the drawer.

examples.ko: 밤에 부엌에서 달그락 소리가 들려서 깼어요.
examples.en: I woke up because I heard a clattering sound in the kitchen at night.
The child dropped the spoon with a clatter.

examples.ko: 열쇠 꾸러미가 가방 안에서 달그락 흔들려요.
examples.en: The bunch of keys rattles around in the bag.
I heard a clatter and turned around, and it was the cat.

explain: 작고 단단한 물건끼리 가볍게 부딪히는 소리예요. 더 크고 무거운 느낌은 '덜그럭'으로 말해요. 보통 '달그락 소리'나 '달그락거리다/달그락대다'로 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is the sound of small hard objects knocking lightly together. For a bigger, heavier sound, people say '덜그럭'. It is often used as '달그락 소리' or in '달그락거리다/달그락대다'.

examples.en: Someone is clattering dishes in the kitchen.

examples.ko: 주머니 속 동전이 걸을 때마다 달그락대요.
examples.en: The coins in my pocket rattle every time I walk.
Since morning, there has been a clattering sound from next door.
I clattered around washing dishes, and the baby woke up.
Please tidy up quietly without clattering.
The child is putting away toys, making a clatter.

explain: '달그락거리다'와 거의 같고 말할 때는 둘 다 써요. 소리를 내는 주어는 물건일 수도, 물건을 만지는 사람일 수도 있어요. 더 큰 소리는 '덜그럭대다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is almost the same as '달그락거리다', and people use both when speaking. The subject can be the objects or the person handling them. For a bigger sound, you say '덜그럭대다'.
